title: UAP Thematic Research Map
limitations: Rows are reference clusters and may bundle multiple publications.
Mappings and scores are analyst judgments, not probabilities or independent confirmation.
Bibliographic identifiers, direct quotations, page references, peer-review status, and replication status require verification.
Established science, observational resemblance, and speculative engineering application must remain separate evidence classes.

references.about: Proposes ball lightning from oxidation of soil-derived nanoparticles after lightning strikes. Highlights conductive silica/carbon networks that self-sustain luminous globes for seconds–minutes. Provides a naturalistic plasma-chemical route to long-lived aerial luminescence.
references.boundary_interpretation: Explains transient halos/filaments akin to shell-like fringes, but not the persistent, pane-like stratified layers or trans-medium entries without turbulence you document. Primarily addresses stochastic, ground-linked events rather than coherent airborne field structures.
references.srms_interpretation: Shows how energetic plasma states can self-stabilize, yet lacks field-resonant control. SRMS would extend beyond chemistry to resonance-driven stability enabling repeatable, drag-free maneuvering instead of rare natural occurrences.
references.theme: Plasma, Ball Lightning & Atmospheric Luminous Phenomena

references.about: Explores theoretical/experimental models of ball lightning with electromagnetic self-confinement and oscillatory feedback. Positions plasmas as self-organizing resonant entities in natural contexts.
references.boundary_interpretation: Self-confinement and oscillatory shells partially support stratified laminar structures seen in boundary-layer frames. Luminous shells, flickering envelopes, and interference-like fringes echo layered observations, yet remain unstable versus your repeatable pane-phase transitions.
references.srms_interpretation: Suggests field-oscillation feedback as a precursor to engineered resonance. SRMS aims to convert stochastic short-lived confinement into tuned, long-duration resonant states powering trans-medium motion.
references.theme: Plasma, Ball Lightning & Atmospheric Luminous Phenomena

references.about: Monograph compiling hundreds of ball lightning cases, durations, color variability, and interactions with structures. Benchmarks diversity and heterogeneity; difficult to unify under a single model.
references.boundary_interpretation: Recurring halos and coherent outlines support the presence of luminous boundary sheaths. However, not framed as aerodynamic boundary-layer substitutes or as indicators of trans-medium stability.
references.srms_interpretation: Serves as a natural database of luminous structures for SRMS comparison. SRMS posits engineered resonance to achieve stability/control beyond spontaneous plasmas.
references.theme: Plasma, Ball Lightning & Atmospheric Luminous Phenomena

references.about: Reports anomalous ball lightning interactions with solids, including glass penetration without damage. Argues for exotic boundary coupling mechanisms.
references.boundary_interpretation: Strongly resonates with pane-phase ‘membrane traversal’—objects passing through media without disturbance—paralleling indexed boundary layers.
references.srms_interpretation: Suggests controlled scalar-resonant fields could replicate membrane-like traversal. Phenomenological precedent for SRMS boundary coupling and field-index modulation.
references.theme: Plasma, Ball Lightning & Atmospheric Luminous Phenomena

references.about: Review of transient luminous events (sprites, elves, halos) with observational/modeling perspectives. Shows turbulence, charge distribution, and instabilities generating complex luminous geometries.
references.boundary_interpretation: Accounts for wake suppression and luminous halos in plasma regimes, but not coherent pane-layered shells or structured axial emissions seen in your cases.
references.srms_interpretation: Establishes a plasma baseline model. SRMS differs by resonance-driven organization producing coherent, repeatable structures beyond random atmospheric instabilities.
references.theme: Plasma, Ball Lightning & Atmospheric Luminous Phenomena

references.about: Observational/theoretical studies offering quantitative estimates of size, luminosity, and motion for UAP. Argue for structured, energy-rich plasma-like phenomena.
references.boundary_interpretation: Quantitative evidence of luminous stratification and localized warping supports nested-shell typology. Persistence and reproducibility echo repeatable laminar structures.
references.srms_interpretation: Provides observational test cases with measurable parameters to evaluate SRMS claims of resonant mobility and structural coherence.
references.theme: Plasma, Ball Lightning & Atmospheric Luminous Phenomena

references.about: Proposes Hessdalen lights via subsoil geophysical interactions and EM fields, linking mineralogy with plasma generation. Frames Hessdalen as an environmental plasma laboratory.
references.boundary_interpretation: Resonates with ‘transition interval’ sheaths where local conditions foster luminous halos. Does not fully explain symmetric layering or drag-free signatures.
references.srms_interpretation: Shows natural resonance conditions can foster plasma anomalies; SRMS extends by asserting controllable field tuning for stable craft dynamics.
references.theme: Plasma, Ball Lightning & Atmospheric Luminous Phenomena

references.about: Long-term monitoring with optical/spectroscopic/radio instrumentation reveals periodicities, emission lines, dynamic structuring indicative of non-random processes.
references.boundary_interpretation: Phase-locked periodicities and structured luminous envelopes support nested laminar shells and oscillatory sheaths; phenomena carry measurable signatures beyond artefacts.
references.srms_interpretation: Suggests resonance as organizing principle; SRMS posits scalar-field resonance driving mobility—natural analogues of engineered resonance states.
references.theme: Plasma, Ball Lightning & Atmospheric Luminous Phenomena

references.about: Broad synthesis linking plasma states, UAP manifestations, and speculative aerospace connections. Positions plasma as a unifying explanatory medium.
references.boundary_interpretation: Explains halos and transient luminous states but not absence of inertial signatures or pane-layer transitions with symmetric axial discharges.
references.srms_interpretation: Sets a plasma baseline that SRMS must surpass by introducing scalar resonance for controllable, high-performance maneuvering.
references.theme: Plasma, Ball Lightning & Atmospheric Luminous Phenomena

references.about: Foundational review of gravitational lensing—mathematics for weak/strong regimes and reconstruction of lens potentials. Gold-standard baseline for curvature-induced optical effects.
references.boundary_interpretation: Boundary frames show localized warping near luminous objects; this provides the control model. If warps occur without sufficient mass, they indicate a field-index pane rather than a mass lens, motivating lensing observables as probes of near-object structure.
references.srms_interpretation: SRMS posits resonance-induced optical path changes; the formalism quantifies deviations from GR expectations as evidence of resonant scalar coupling and enables parameterized testing.
references.theme: Gravitational Lensing, Modified Gravity & Optical Scalars

references.about: Optical scalar (Sachs) formalism—expansion, shear, twist—to describe light-bundle evolution in curved or refractive media. Sensitive to local gradients and rapid distortions.
references.boundary_interpretation: Maps to localized dilation, directional stretching, and transient rotation near boundaries. Enables encoding of boundary-layer signatures as time series of optical scalars.
references.srms_interpretation: SRMS uses tunable index landscapes; optical scalars measure how engineered fields steer light. Suggests phase-sensitive experiments keyed to drive frequency.
references.theme: Gravitational Lensing, Modified Gravity & Optical Scalars

references.about: Explores extreme lensing scenarios (e.g., naked singularities) with distinctive image morphologies as guides to nonstandard metrics.
references.boundary_interpretation: Abrupt appearance/disappearance and odd arcs can arise from exotic effective geometries; supports treating boundaries as effective metrics with distinctive caustics.
references.srms_interpretation: Small geometry changes yield large optical consequences—motivates SRMS tuning for cloaking/displacement without mass relocation; image topology becomes a diagnostic.
references.theme: Gravitational Lensing, Modified Gravity & Optical Scalars

references.about: Alternative gravity work shows added fields can modify light propagation without large unseen mass, opening scalar/tensor extensions as optics actors.
references.boundary_interpretation: Supports field-mediated deflections consistent with pane-layer sheaths controlling local refraction absent mass concentrations.
references.srms_interpretation: SRMS applies this principle at craft scale: scalar resonance sets index profiles dynamically, achieving lensing/cloaking effects on demand.
references.theme: Gravitational Lensing, Modified Gravity & Optical Scalars

references.about: Galilean-invariant scalar fields with screening enabling strong local effects while evading cosmological limits; gradients matter.
references.boundary_interpretation: Thin laminar sheaths with sharp gradients fit screened scalar zones, not volumetric lenses—consistent with observed pane signatures.
references.srms_interpretation: Confined, resonant scalar energy in engineered membranes is plausible; points to parameter ranges SRMS can target for strong local optics with weak far-field signatures.
references.theme: Gravitational Lensing, Modified Gravity & Optical Scalars

references.boundary_interpretation: Frame-by-frame inversions can reveal persistent localized gradients at the pane, turning qualitative warps into rigorous reconstructions.
references.srms_interpretation: Pipelines verify SRMS: recover effective deflection maps under different resonance states and compare to SRMS simulations to estimate index contrast and potential depth.

references.srms_interpretation: SRMS can adopt these transfer functions as target effective optics for its resonance layer, informing control laws for specific cloaking/displacement modes.

references.about: Optical conformal mapping steers rays via geometric transformations; translates desired geometry into refractive-index blueprints—pillar of transformation optics.
references.boundary_interpretation: Pane regions producing local lensing and outline suppression map to Leonhardt-style index profiles concentrated in thin sheaths; explains disappear/reappear edges and muted wakes.
references.srms_interpretation: SRMS uses scalar-resonant fields to instantiate those index maps dynamically; the framework supplies target optical effects while SRMS provides the control law.

references.about: Canonical invisibility cloak via spatially varying anisotropic ε/μ in metamaterials; bends rays around a volume with minimal scattering—engineering target.
references.boundary_interpretation: Recorded edge suppression and refractive warping resemble cloak phenomenology; your thin energetic sheath stands in for bulky metamaterial shells.
references.srms_interpretation: SRMS reframes cloak as a field-programmable boundary where resonant membranes reproduce effective ε/μ distributions without physical lattices.

references.about: Extends cloaking to full-wave regimes and broader PDE contexts; clarifies uniqueness and limitations—mathematical foundation for ideal cloaks.
references.boundary_interpretation: Explains transient invisibility and reappearance as tuning between admissible parameter ranges; shimmering edges indicate mis-tuning near boundary conditions.
references.srms_interpretation: Defines SRMS stability corridors; controllers must keep resonance within cloaking-eligible bands during maneuvers.

references.about: Survey of resonant cloaking and scattering cancellation across polar/thermal/acoustic metamaterials; generalizes transparency via resonance.
references.boundary_interpretation: Observed scattering suppression (edge fade, outline compression) matches resonance-assisted cancellation in thin sheaths during dynamic motion.
references.srms_interpretation: SRMS is resonance-centric, targeting cancellation modes across optical/RF/aero-acoustic channels during high-speed turns.

references.about: Thermal/diffusive analogues of cloaking via transformation principles; proves multiphysics hiding beyond light.
references.boundary_interpretation: Multiphyics cloaking parallels panes acting on light, air flow, and thermal gradients—explains muted wakes and lack of shock signatures.
references.srms_interpretation: SRMS aims for a single resonant field modulating multiple transport properties simultaneously—composite objectives for trans-medium maneuvers.

references.about: Review of broadband cloaking in architected metamaterials, stressing robustness and hybrid passive–active strategies from lab to systems.
references.boundary_interpretation: Your observations imply broadband, rapid-response behavior—beyond narrowband passive cloaks—necessitating active control and reconfiguration on the fly.
references.srms_interpretation: SRMS matches the hybrid-active motif: scalar resonant membranes continually re-tune to maintain low scattering across changing conditions; provides KPIs (bandwidth, latency, stability).

references.about: ZPF-based accounts of inertia and vacuum engineering; reframes inertia as emergent from vacuum fluctuations and suggests pathways to manipulate vacuum–matter coupling.
references.boundary_interpretation: Supports drag-free transitions and sudden accelerations without wakes if inertial coupling can be gated at the sheath/pane.
references.srms_interpretation: SRMS extends by using scalar resonance as a local control knob for inertia coupling, turning conceptual vacuum engineering into tunable mobility states.

references.about: Field resonance propulsion and surveys of non-conventional electrokinetic concepts; proposes oscillatory fields as propulsion channels beyond rockets.

references.srms_interpretation: SRMS specifies the operative channel—scalar resonance—providing physical substrate and testable parameters the early concepts lacked.

references.about: Replications/limit tests on alleged EM–gravity couplings with stringent null results; sets careful experimental constraints.

references.srms_interpretation: Frames SRMS as a distinct, testable mechanism (scalar resonance) with effects above detection thresholds and separable from failed EM–gravity claims.
